ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation and continuous screening of all shareholders, directors, officers and beneficial owners against the Swiss SECO sanctions lists, Swiss State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO) financial sanctions, UN Security Council Consolidated List, US OFAC SDN and non-SDN sanctions, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, and the Swiss Federal Criminal Police (fedpol) PEP database. Any politically exposed person (PEP) is subject to enhanced due diligence, including source-of-wealth verification and senior management approval. Screening results must be recorded and documented for at least ten years under AMLA record-keeping obligations.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zentraler Firmenindex (ZEFIX), the official Swiss commercial registry name index, operated by the Federal Department of Justice and Police in cooperation with cantonal commercial register offices; available at www.zefix.ch
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be lawful, truthful, clear and not misleading under Articles 950 and 951 OR. The formal registry entry must use a Swiss national language (German, French, Italian or Romansh) and Latin script. Foreign-language names and transliterated non-Latin script names are accepted only where they are not misleading and are accompanied by the mandatory Swiss legal suffix 'AG' / 'SA'. The name must not suggest public authority or a connection with the Swiss Confederation unless specifically authorised.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If a name is rejected, the commercial register office serves a written negative notice stating the legal grounds. The applicant may file an administrative appeal within 30 days with the competent cantonal supervisory authority (in the Canton of Zurich: the Directorate of Justice and the Interior), and ultimately with the Swiss Federal Administrative Court in St. Gallen under Articles 44–60 VwVG. Alternatively, the applicant may immediately submit an amended name for a fresh preliminary review; correction of the prohibited or misleading token normally resolves the refusal. A name reservation may not be automatically extended, but a fresh reservation period begins upon resubmission of a revised, compliant name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A purely virtual or mail-forwarding address is not permissible as the sole registered office of a Swiss stock company (AG), because the registered office must be a real location of administration where corporate records are accessible and from which the company is actually managed. For the present low-risk Amazon FBA general e-commerce business, a shared business-centre or fiduciary service address may be tolerated only if a physical presence, access to books, and a named local authorised person are contractually secured. Any virtual office arrangement without administrative substance creates a live risk of commercial register cancellation and re-characterisation for tax or regulatory purposes.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low: approximately 5% annual probability of unannounced physical inspection for a standard, non-licensed low-risk e-commerce entity with a genuine registered office and regular UBO documentation. The likelihood increases to 10–15% if a virtual address, nominee directors, bearer-share structures, or incomplete beneficial ownership records are detected. Cantonal commercial register offices, tax authorities, and financial intermediaries conducting AMLA compliance reviews each have legal power to require documentary and on-site verification.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht/Code des obligations, CO), Articles 620–626 (formation and capital requirements of the Aktiengesellschaft), Article 629 (minimum share capital), Article 631 (notarial deed requirement), Article 640 (registration in the Commercial Register), and the Swiss Federal Ordinance on the Commercial Register (Handelsregisterverordnung, HRegV), Articles 5–25
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Register of the Canton of Zurich (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zürich), acting as the cantonal agency of the Federal Commercial Register administered by the Federal Department of Justice and Police
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation Declaration (Erklärung zur Gründung / Déclaration de constitution) executed by notarial deed, accompanied by the Articles of Association (Statuten) and the application for registration in the Commercial Register (Anmeldung zur Eintragung)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Share capital must amount to at least CHF 100,000, fully subscribed at incorporation; a minimum of CHF 50,000 must be paid up in cash and confirmed by a bank attestation of unrestricted credit or by an audited in-kind contribution; the paid-up capital must remain blocked in the company's bank account until Commercial Register registration is completed
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporation of the Company under Articles 620–626 of the Swiss Code of Obligations is hereby confirmed; that the share subscriptions totaling CHF 100,000 nominal capital are accepted and the bank attestation confirming the minimum paid-up capital of CHF 50,000 is verified; that the registered office of the Company be located at [registered address], Canton of Zurich; that the Articles of Association, as presented, are approved and submitted to the Commercial Register; and that [First Name Last Name] and [First Name Last Name] are appointed as Directors, each holding the power of sole signature. The Directors are authorized to execute all registration filings, open operating and payment-acquirer accounts with Amazon Pay, Stripe, and Airwallex, and engage the statutory auditor.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening and Release of Blocked Paid-Up Capital Attestation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Swiss bank designated by the founding shareholders (e.g., UBS AG, Credit Suisse, Zürcher Kantonalbank)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct the chosen bank to open a corporate account in the future company name and deposit the minimum paid-up capital of CHF 50,000 (or the full CHF 100,000). Provide the bank with the draft Articles of Association, beneficial ownership declaration, source-of-funds documentation, and the collective signature mandate. The bank issues a formal attestation (Liberierungsbescheinigung) confirming that the funds are at the company's free disposal but are contractually blocked (Sperrvermerk) until the Commercial Register registration is completed. On the same day, cause each founder to execute the share subscription statement for the remaining unpaid portion, if any.
required_dossiers: Certified passport copies of all founders and beneficial owners
Proof of residential address for each shareholder
Draft Articles of Association in German or French
Source-of-funds declarations and bank references meeting the Anti-Money Laundering Act (GwG)
Completed bank beneficial-ownership and tax-residency (FATCA/CRS) forms
Business description confirming ISIC 4791 cross-border marketplace activity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank declines the attestation due to incomplete KYC, supplement the file with origin-of-wealth affidavits and certified bank references; for escalated queries, escalate to the bank's commercial-desk compliance officer and provide the registry-compliant blocking wording in line with Art. 629 CO; if the bank cannot deliver within instructed time, substitute a cantonal bank licensed under Swiss banking law.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Legal Review of Articles of Association and Notarial Instructions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Swiss notary public (Notariat) in the Canton of Zurich, with pre-clearance by a resident Swiss corporate attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the statutory deed containing the Articles of Association (Statuten). The Articles must set the full corporate name with legal-form indicator AG, registered office (Canton Zurich), purpose limited to e-commerce marketplace retail and cross-border distribution of consumer goods, nominal share capital of CHF 100,000 with registered shares, board composition, quorum rules, and auditor selection. Convene the founding shareholders for a notarial meeting; each subscriber must appear personally or by notarized proxy before the notary. The notary authenticates the incorporation declaration and the initial statement of the founders confirming paid-up contributions. Immediately thereafter circulate the notarial protocol to the Cantonal Tax Office (Steueramt) and reserve the company name through the Swiss Name Reservation system (Zefix pre-check).
required_dossiers: Articles of Association in German (bilingual French/English certified translation optional)
Notary appointment confirmation and fees disclosure
Shareholder resolutions on subscribed capital allocation
Shareholder passport copies and Swiss residence attestations (not required but recommended)
Name reservation token from Zefix for 'CH AG'
Bank proof of paid-up capital attestation from Step 1
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or the competent authority objects to a statutory clause, the attorneys must revise the relevant Article (e.g., purpose clause) and have the founders sign an addendum; if the chosen company name is rejected or collides with a registered trademark, apply for an alternative name through Zefix on the same day; all revisions are re-notarized with no additional monetary fine beyond the notary statutory scale.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarial Execution of the Incorporation Deed and Verifiability of Contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Notary Public of Zurich; verification office (Anttliche Bewertung) for in-kind contributions, if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: At the notarial closing, the founders execute the incorporation deed confirming that: the full CHF 100,000 nominal capital has been subscribed; the paid-up capital of CHF 50,000 (or higher) is evidenced by the bank attestation; and any non-cash contribution is covered by a sworn report of the auditor with an assessed value not exceeding CHF 50,000. The notary then certifies the deed, assigns the deed number, and issues the official notarial copy (Ausfertigung) including the statutory signature specimens (Unterschriftsproben) of all directors for the Commercial Register filing. The notary also confirms the completion of the declaration of incorporation and transmits the certified dossier to the Commercial Register Office.
required_dossiers: Executed incorporation deed and notarized Articles of Association
Bank release attestation for paid-up capital
Auditor report for in-kind contributions (if non-cash)
Certificate of name reservation and official name prior-art check
Declaration of the Board accepting office and specimen signatures
List of registered shareholders with capital split and voting rights
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Should the notary identify a capital shortfall or mismatched contribution values, deposit the corrective cash amount into the blocked account and reissue the attestation before signing; if the deed requires alterations due to registry queries, execute a supplementary protocol and annex it to the original deed within 10 days under Art. 14 HRegV.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Register Application and Statutory Publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zurich (Handelsregisteramt), Federal Commercial Register (Zefix/EBR system)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the application for registration using the official 'Anmeldung zur Eintragung' form, attaching the notarized incorporation deed, Articles of Association, list of directors with sole-signature authority, specimen signatures, and the bank attestation. The Commercial Register is prescribed to review within 5 days of filing. Upon approval, the company is registered with legal personality effective as of the date of entry. The office forwards the entry for mandatory publication in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB), which gives effect to the company's legal existence vis-à-vis third parties. The registration number (Zefix-ID) and the Canton Zurich VAT and commercial identification codes are issued simultaneously.
required_dossiers: Official registration application form signed by all directors
Notarized deed of incorporation with original notary seal
Verified Articles of Association including legal form indicator and purpose clause
Statutory declaration of paid-up and subscribed capital
Board minutes including officer appointments and signature authority disclosure
Source-of-funds attestation for the paid-up capital, including bank confirmation
Power of attorney if filing through a notary representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a provisional refusal or query, within 30 days under Art. 8b HRegV provide the required clarifications (e.g., corrected signature specimen or explicit approval of the Articles by the competent tax authority); if the principal place of business is found incomplete, submit the registered office address certificate from the municipal residents' office; should the appeal be unfounded, the applicants may file for court direction with the Cantonal Civil Court (Commercial Register supervision division).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal and Cantonal Fiscal-Relevant Post-Incorporation Filings and Employment Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Tax Office Zurich (Steueramt Zürich), Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA), Swiss Compensation Office (Ausgleichskasse), and Cantonal Labor Inspectorate
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration, complete the mandatory registrations: (i) file the corporate tax registration with the Cantonal Tax Office for corporate income tax and net wealth tax assessment; (ii) register for VAT with the Federal Tax Administration if worldwide turnover exceeds CHF 100,000 (Swiss VAT Act Art. 10) or if cross-border digital services are supplied — the company will obtain a Swiss VAT registry number; (iii) accede to the Cantonal Compensation Office as the employer for social security (AHV/IV/EO) for directors and staff; (iv) file the accident-insurance declaration with SUVA; and (v) register the e-commerce activity with the Cantonal Labor Inspectorate under the collective employment and workplace safety rules. The Amazon FBA business model implies no sectoral license, but the company must register its warehouse premises with the municipal building authority for occupancy purposes.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Commercial Register registration (Extrait du registre du commerce / Handelsregisterauszug)
Zefix registration excerpt
Canton Zurich tax declaration for economic domicile
VAT registration form no. 102 (Questionário for Swiss VAT)
Employer registration forms AHV 01/03 for board and employees
Fire safety and occupancy clearance for warehouse/office premises
Evidence of corporate bank account with payment-rail activation for Amazon Pay, Stripe, and Airwallex
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the Cantonal Tax Office advises a late registration penalty, submit the company founding receipts and registry certificate to evidence force majeure; if the VAT registration is delayed for cross-border supplies, pay the minimal undeclared VAT with zero-interest adjustment within the 60-day cure window of Art. 70 VAT Act; missing social-insurance registrations are cured by retroactive contribution payment plus a fixed surcharge, without criminal penalty if disclosed voluntarily.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO) with execution delegated to the Cantonal Labor Inspectorate Zurich (Amt für Arbeit) and the Cantonal Department of Trade (Volkswirtschaftsdirektion) — no sectoral license applies to ISIC 4791 e-commerce retail
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: E-commerce marketplace retail is a non-licensed activity under Swiss law; the company will file a municipal trade notification (Gewerbemeldung) to the Cantonal Trade Office and obtain a warehouse occupancy permit (Grundmeldung der Betriebsstätte) under the Cantonal Building Code; this administrative certification confirms compliance without a sectoral operating license on the federal level

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (Bundesamt für Umwelt, BAFU/FOEN), with cantonal environmental enforcement for warehouse logistics below federal thresholds
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration / Exempt — the standard Amazon FBA logistics warehouse with floor area below 5,000 m² and without internal combustion systems is not subject to a mandatory full Environmental Impact Assessment under Annex 1 of the EIA Ordinance (UVPV); a cantonal environmental self-monitoring declaration and valid waste-handling agreement apply
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: discharge of cooling / sanitary water into the municipal sewer network must comply with the Water Protection Ordinance (GSchV) maximum permissible concentrations (e.g., pH 6.5–9.0, COD ≤ 600 mg/L); VOCs: packaging printing and labeling applications, if on-site, must conform with the VOC Ordinance (VOCV) maximum limit of 20 mg/Nm³; general waste: logistics waste, cardboard, and returned goods must be segregated and recycled in accordance with the Technical Ordinance on Municipal Waste (TVA), and dangerous goods (electronics, aerosols) must be declared to the cantonal waste service
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate (Brandschutznachweis) issued by the Cantonal Fire Protection Police under the VKF Fire Protection Regulations, based on a floor-plan review and a one-time structural load inspection by a certified engineer; workplace clearance issued by the Cantonal Labor Inspectorate for the fulfillment of workspaces, ventilation, and sanitary areas under the Swiss Workplace Ordinance (ASV); the company must also carry out a SUVA workplace occupational-safety risk assessment for warehouse height, racking stability, and conveyor systems

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung ESTV / Administration fédérale des contributions AFC / Amministrazione federale delle contribuzioni AFC); official portal: https://www.estv.admin.ch; VAT registration and e-filing portal: https://www.estv.admin.ch/en/home/mehrwertsteuer.html; Swiss business identifier (UID) register administered by the Federal Statistical Office via https://www.uid.admin.ch.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 – Determine nexus: a foreign entity must register for Swiss VAT if its annual worldwide turnover reaches CHF 100,000 or if its taxable supplies in Switzerland exceed CHF 100,000 per calendar year (Art. 10 para 2(a) VAT Act, MWSTG). For Amazon FBA sellers without a Swiss establishment, the marketplace deemed-supplier rules from 1 January 2025 may in certain consignment-stock and low-value import scenarios shift the Swiss VAT liability to Amazon. Step 2 – Appoint a Swiss fiscal representative (Art. 67 MWSTG): a foreign company not resident in Switzerland and without a Swiss permanent establishment must appoint a domiciled representative in Switzerland (typically a fiduciary or tax adviser) who is jointly and severally liable for the VAT. Step 3 – Obtain a Swiss UID business identifier (format CHE-XXX.XXX.XXX) for the foreign entity via the UID register; no Swiss commercial register (Handelsregister) entry is required for the foreign entity itself. Step 4 – File the VAT registration application with the Federal Tax Administration through the official VAT e-services portal, attaching: the UID confirmation, a home-country commercial register extract (with certified German/French/Italian translation if needed), a power of attorney granted to the Swiss fiscal representative, a description of the marketplace e-commerce activity (ISIC 4791 / NAICS 454110), and projected Swiss turnover. Step 5 – After approval, the FTA issues the VAT number consisting of the UID plus the 'MWST' suffix (e.g., CHE-123.456.789 MWST); the taxpayer then files periodic (usually quarterly) VAT returns electronically. The procedure typically takes two to four weeks; registration is retroactive to the date the obligation arose.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. The Swiss Aktiengesellschaft (AG/SA) is a standalone legal person subject to Swiss corporate income tax at the federal, cantonal and communal levels on its worldwide net profit (federal rate 8.5% on profit after federal income tax, equivalent to approximately 7.83% effective), with exemption-with-progression for profits attributable to foreign permanent establishments and foreign real estate. The AG has no pass-through eligibility; shareholders are separately taxed on dividends (partial taxation/participation relief). Territorial_Scope: Swiss resident companies are taxed on worldwide profits, but income from foreign PEs and foreign immovable property is exempt in Switzerland by treaty or domestic practice. Tax_Exempt_Zone: Not applicable; Switzerland maintains no general tax-haven, free-zone or offshore entity regime for active e-commerce operations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Switzerland does not operate a US-style check-the-box classification system; legal form exclusively governs tax status. Available elections: (1) Optional VAT registration for small businesses with annual worldwide turnover below CHF 100,000 (Art. 11 MWSTG), often elected to recover input VAT. (2) Election between the effective input-VAT-deduction method and the flat-rate input-tax method (Saldosteuersatzverfahren, Art. 37 and 38 MWSTG), appropriate for sellers whose input tax is hard to determine precisely. (3) Option under Art. 22 MWSTG to subject otherwise-exempt supplies (e.g., proceeds from sale of immovable property or financial services) to VAT. (4) With respect to hybrid mismatches, Swiss domestic law contains no unilateral entity-election or check-the-box mechanisms; Switzerland addresses hybrid situations primarily through its double-tax-treaty network, the BEPS Multilateral Instrument and published FTA administrative practice, and no domestic 'hybrid election' is available in the Swiss VAT or corporate income tax laws.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Swiss Value Added Tax (Mehrwertsteuer / Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée / Imposta sul valore aggiunto), governed by the Federal Act of 12 June 2009 on Value Added Tax (MWSTG/LTVA), a non-EU harmonised VAT system.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 per calendar year of worldwide turnover (Art. 10 para 2(a) MWSTG); CHF 150,000 for non-profit and amateur-sport entities (Art. 10 para 2(d) MWSTG). Non-established foreign sellers must register when their taxable supplies to persons in Switzerland exceed CHF 100,000 p.a. From 1 January 2025, portal/marketplace operators (including Amazon) are deemed to make the underlying supply for Swiss VAT purposes in respect of (i) distance sales of imported goods with a value not exceeding CHF 150 (low-value consignment relief) and (ii) goods introduced into Switzerland under a consignment-stock scheme; the marketplace operator becomes the VAT debtor for those transactions.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Switzerland imposes no real-time fiscal clearance, no mandatory digital stamping, no government pre-clearance of e-invoices and no mandatory invoice-by-invoice API clearance system. Structured e-invoicing (Peppol BIS 3.0 / B2G) is mandatory only for suppliers issuing invoices to the federal administration since 1 January 2020; B2B e-billing (Peppol network or eBill) remains voluntary. VAT returns must be filed electronically via the FTA's VAT portal (XML/file-transfer/API-based batch submission supported for large taxpayers) within 60 days after the end of the reporting period. Amazon FBA sellers must nonetheless retain full electronic order, dispatch, shipment-tracking and payment XML records sufficient for audit reconstruction.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rated Swiss VAT (0%) applies to physical exports of goods when the seller or a third party on its behalf exports the goods and the buyer obtains the power of disposal abroad (Art. 18 para 2 MWSTG), including Amazon FBA cross-border shipments to non-Swiss customers. Selected services are likewise zero-rated: services relating to movable tangible property that is exported, services relating to foreign immovable property, and B2B services performed abroad for foreign recipients. The supplier must prove the export by the customs export declaration (Ausfuhrzollanmeldung / export data released by the Swiss customs system) or, for hand-carried exports, by the customs officer's written confirmation. Digital and e-services supplied to Swiss private consumers remain taxable at 8.1% (or 2.6% where the reduced rate applies) and cannot be zero-rated merely because the seller is foreign. Refund/input-VAT credit mechanisms apply on the Swiss VAT return where the seller is registered; non-registered foreign sellers may recover Swiss input VAT through the FTA's refund procedure for foreign businesses under Art. 107 MWSTG only, subject to reciprocity.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Ausfuhrzollanmeldung) or electronic customs export data release
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill (ocean, air, postal or combined transport proof to the non-Swiss consignee)
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank credit confirmation evidencing receipt of the export proceeds
Commercial invoice and packing list for the FBA shipment
Amazon seller central shipment records, inbound/outbound warehouse data and final delivery confirmation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Swiss law imposes no statutory 180-day foreign-exchange repatriation deadline for Amazon FBA export proceeds; the 180-day figure is adopted as a documentary audit benchmark consistent with standard export payment terms and FTA practice in reviewing completed export transactions. The Swiss Federal Tax Administration may within ten years (five years in good-faith cases) retrospectively reassess incorrectly zero-rated supplies and claw back any input VAT previously credited; in cases of tax evasion the limitation period is ten years and may be indefinite for fraudulent concealment. On reassessment the taxpayer must pay the under-declared VAT plus default interest (administrative interest of 5% p.a. adjusted periodically) and, if input VAT was improperly credited, reimbursement of that credit. Administrative fines range up to the amount of the evaded tax in simple cases and up to four times the evaded amount in serious cases under Art. 96-101 MWSTG. Intentional VAT fraud is additionally prosecuted under Art. 14 of the Swiss Federal Act on Administrative Criminal Law (VStrR), carrying imprisonment of up to three years or a monetary penalty, and the responsible officers and the Swiss fiscal representative may be held jointly liable.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB; Schweizerische Nationalbank), operating under the National Bank Act (SR 951.11) and the Federal Act on Currency and Payment Instruments (SR 941.10), with supporting oversight by the Federal Department of Finance (FDF) and the State Secretariat for International Financial Matters (SIF).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland imposes no exchange controls; the Swiss franc (CHF) is fully convertible across both current and capital accounts. Dividend, profit, interest, and royalty remittances to non-residents are freely permitted without FX authorization, subject only to ordinary corporate tax, 35% dividend withholding tax (reduced under applicable double tax treaties), and standard bank compliance documentation. No capital account restrictions, retrocessional limitations, or inward investment approval regimes apply to inbound share capital or outbound distributions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export proceeds surrender rule or mandatory conversion ratio applies in Switzerland. Exporters may freely retain receipts in any foreign currency and maintain multi-currency accounts. The only binding obligation is incremental statistical reporting to the SNB under the Financial Statistics Ordinance (SR 951.1) for balance-of-payments compilation, with de minimis thresholds and no repatriation timeline.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (current/multi-currency) and Capital Escrow Account
Operational Account (CHF and multi-currency) with SEPA/SWIFT access
Operational Account and segregated escrow sub-account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility. Foreign digital EMIs and PSPs (e.g., Airwallex, Stripe, Wise) may be engaged as supplementary payment facilitators for marketplace collections, multi-currency conversion, and payout routing, provided they operate through a FINMA-regulated correspondent or partner bank. They are not substitutes for a Swiss banking relationship: without a Swiss banking or FinTech licence under SR 952.02, an offshore EMI may not accept public deposits in Switzerland or hold statutory capital escrow, and the AG must retain a primary account at a Swiss-regulated bank for corporate registration, VAT/statutory audit tracing, and SNB reporting.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No statutory rule universally requires physical director attendance; remote opening is available through video identification and standard e-signature channels for low-risk standard e-commerce structures with a Swiss-resident beneficial owner. However, Swiss banks retain risk-based discretion: in-person or additional interactive video interviews are effectively mandated where directors are non-resident, where the UBO is domiciled in a high-risk or non-cooperative jurisdiction, or where the account class involves credit facilities or escrow arrangements. Best practice is to schedule one physical or video executive interview with the authorized signatories and to evidence the commercial substance of the Amazon FBA operation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: marketplace-driven high-volume micro-payment flows inconsistent with declared turnover and VAT filings.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited or reviewed annual financial statements, Swiss VAT returns and proof of VAT registration, Amazon Seller Central 30-day settlement reports, platform seller service agreement, and a reconciling cash-flow schedule tracing all marketplace disbursements to bank credits.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: non-resident director or foreign-resident UBO with opaque source of funds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized passport and proof of address, curriculum vitae and professional references, source-of-wealth statement with supporting bank or asset documentation, Swiss Commercial Register excerpt confirming AG formation, and confirmation of the economic purpose of the Swiss holding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: third-party payer concentration and cross-border counterparty patterns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Amazon Payments and FBA distribution agreements, executed supplier invoices with Incoterms, logistics contracts, and, where applicable, evidence of SEPA/SWIFT routing through named professional counterparties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: use of digital EMIs or crypto-adjacent settlement rails for receipts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid contractual engagement letters with licensed PSPs, FINMA correspondence on any crowdfunding or FinTech permits, transaction-level audit trails, and board-approved treasury policy restricting crypto conversion to FINMA-compliant channels.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity injections are executed via SWIFT MT103 or MT202 from the parent or investor with clear purpose coding (e.g., share capital contribution or equity injection), referencing the reserved share capital resolution of the board. No SNB approval or exchange control permit is required; banks request proof of source of funds, the share register, and the notarized capital increase deed. Multi-currency inbound wires may be credited to a CHF or foreign-currency account and converted intra-bank at commercial rates. SNB statistical forms (balance-of-payments surveys) apply above reporting thresholds.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements should be cleared through SWIFT gpi-qualified MT103 for supplier payments, confirmed or unconfirmed Commercial Letters of Credit governed by UCP600 for large purchase orders, and SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant for EU-based vendors. Amazon FBA payouts are routed through the marketplace via Amazon Pay, Stripe, or Airwallex into the operational account, thereafter re-positioned for supplier disbursement, inventory replenishment, VAT payments, and treasury sweeps. Same-day liquidity coverage should be maintained through intraday liquidity buffers and cleared via SIC (Swiss Interbank Clearing) for the domestic leg settlement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX Forwards (deliverable, CHF/EUR/USD and G10 crosses)
Cross-Currency Swaps (FX swaps and long-dated cross-currency basis swaps)
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for restricted or illiquid emerging-market currencies (e.g., CNY/CNH, INR, IDR, BRL) processed through Swiss bank trading desks

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements, statutory audit report (if applicable), and approval by the Annual General Meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Meeting of Shareholders under Art. 699 and 728 CO; no filing to the commercial register is required for ordinary parity AGs
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the balance-sheet date, unless the articles of association set a shorter term
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Civil liability of the Board of Directors under Art. 754 CO; shareholders may petition the court to convene the meeting; no automatic administrative strike-off, but insolvent or non-manageable companies can be dissolved by the commercial register office under Art. 731b CO

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual federal, cantonal, and communal income tax return (Steuererklärung) with capital tax declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Administration at the registered office, acting for cantonal and federal direct taxes, with Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) as federal authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Calendar-year companies must generally file by 31 March to 31 May of the following year; automatic extensions up to 30 June and further 3–6 month extensions are available on request from the cantonal tax authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest at 4% p.a. on unpaid taxes from maturity; procedural fines up to CHF 10,000 under Art. 174 of the Federal Act on Direct Federal Tax; estimated assessment and enforced collection if no return is filed; no automatic deregistration, but persistent non-payment can lead to bankruptcy and deletion from the commercial register

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the end of each VAT period; the standard period is the calendar quarter for businesses with annual turnover exceeding CHF 100,000; smaller businesses may use an annual period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest at the statutory default rate; administrative fines under the Swiss Value Added Tax Act for late or incomplete filings; tax authority may estimate the tax base and commence coercive collection; no administrative strike-off solely for VAT delinquency

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual employer wage declaration and AHV/AVS contribution statement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within 30 days after the annual request from the compensation office, typically by late January for calendar-year payroll data; AHV/AVS contributions are payable quarterly
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest on overdue contributions and administrative fines under Art. 86 AHVG; the compensation office may refuse contribution certificates and institute enforcement against employer assets; no commercial-register strike-off is triggered

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual review and confirmation of share register and beneficial-owner register entries
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Board of Directors and auditors; register must be available to tax authorities and AML supervisors upon request; no annual filing is submitted to a government registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At every balance-sheet date and promptly upon any acquisition, transfer, or change of beneficial ownership of shares
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: False entries and omissions are punishable by fines under Art. 697m CO and may render directors personally liable for resulting loss; incomplete registers do not by themselves cause commercial-register strike-off

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An ordinary (full) statutory audit is mandatory under Art. 727 CO when the company exceeds two of the following three thresholds in two consecutive fiscal years: balance sheet total CHF 20,000,000; turnover CHF 40,000,000; average annual headcount 250 full-time employees. Companies not requiring an ordinary audit are subject to a limited audit unless the shareholders unanimously waive the audit, which is possible only when the company has no more than 10 full-time employees on annual average.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations, Art. 957–958f (OR accounting requirements) as the binding minimum; Swiss GAAP FER is commonly applied as a recognized framework; IFRS is permitted and may be required for listed or regulated entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Switzerland does not require a public or government-filed annual UBO return. Under Art. 697i et seq. CO, the company must maintain an internal beneficial-owner register and a share register. The Board must annually review these registers, obtain confirmations from shareholders when direct or indirect ownership changes, and record transfers promptly. False or incomplete UBO declarations are subject to fines under Art. 697m CO.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Authorized Signatories (Verwaltungsrat / Zeichnungsberechtigte)
Minute Book (minutes of the Board of Directors and General Meeting)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 450 – USD 1,500 per year for registered office and corporate agent services in Zug, Zurich, or Geneva
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 – USD 25,000 for a limited audit; USD 30,000 – USD 80,000 for a full statutory ordinary audit

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 8.5% federal corporate income tax rate (effective federal burden 7.83% after deductibility of the federal tax itself); combined federal plus Zug cantonal/communal headline profit tax for a trading Aktiengesellschaft is approximately 14.6% of pre-tax profit.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory tax holiday exists. Zug ruling practice grants notional interest deduction on qualified excess equity, preferential factor allocation for minimal-risk Amazon FBA distribution functions, and participation relief (Beteiligungsabzug) exempting dividends and capital gains from qualifying participations of at least 10% or CHF 1,000,000 book value. Federal and Zug patent/IP-box regimes are not available for e-commerce trading income; ordinary arm's length deductions for royalties, logistics and fulfillment costs apply.
